text:
aisha: Heads up — starting ~07:12 UTC we saw a spike of 502s and connection resets on model fetches from our us-west-2 edge pool. App logs show a lot of ECONNRESET when contacting S3/model-store and metric spikes on NAT.
matt: Yep saw the same. Strange pattern: many sockets stuck in TIME_WAIT on the NAT side and higher than usual ephemeral port allocation. CloudWatch NATGateway metrics show a sudden jump in ActiveConnections + PortAllocation errors.
infra-bot: CloudWatch link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/cloudwatch/home?region=us-west-2#dashboards:name=egress-nat-overview (recent graphs: NATGatewayBytesOut + NATGatewayActiveFlowCount both spiked)
aisha: Quick diagnostic I ran on one affected node:
```
ss -s
netstat -anp | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l  # ~38k
conntrack -S
```
Shows huge TIME_WAIT backlog, many short-lived outbound connections to S3 and our telemetry collector.
sam: Any chance kube-proxy or a sidecar is creating new outbound connections per request (no keepalive)? We've seen similar after a client bump that removed pooling.
oliver: Confirmed — sidecar image-puller in the edge pool switched to concurrent downloads last week (PR #1123). It opens a fresh connection per shard; combined with 1200 pods across AZ we blow ephemeral port space quickly.
matt: AWS NAT Gateway effectively gives ~64k source ports per NAT IP. If many flows come from same NAT IP, you hit exhaustion. We have ~2 NAT gateways in the AZ but most nodes route to the same one. That explains the rapid exhaustion.
sre-oncall: Impact: request failures to S3/model-store -> model load failures -> 502 to clients. Also we get retries that multiply connections.
aisha: Immediate mitigation options:
- throttle concurrent pulls in the sidecar (patch rollout)
- move model pulls through an internal pooling proxy (short-term)
- add a dedicated NAT gateway(s) and split node subnets across them
- configure S3 VPC Gateway endpoint for model-store (removes NAT entirely)
matt: Quick commands to detect which nodes are hitting the NAT hard:
```
# on each node
ss -tanp | grep ESTAB | awk '{print $5}' | cut -d: -f1 | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head
# check egress IPs seen by NAT (from VPC flow logs / NAT logs)
```
sam: Short-term I can roll a hotfix to the sidecar restricting concurrency and re-enable connection pooling (HTTP/1.1 keepalive). That should drop ephemeral port churn by ~80%.
oliver: I'll prepare a runbook to split high-egress nodes into a distinct subnet and route that subnet to a new NAT gateway. That buys more port space without touching apps.
infra-bot: Inc created: INC-2026-1782. Alerting rule silenced for noisy retries, but will keep paged for saturation metrics.
aisha: Perf note — we should also consider an HTTP egress proxy (squid/nginx) as a short-lived pooler for downloads and model pulls. Easier than changing all clients.
matt: Longer-term: add S3 VPC endpoint for model-store + enforce egress IP pools for heavy clients. Also consider switching heavy telemetry to Kinesis Firehose over VPC endpoint.
sre-oncall: Action items & owners:
- sam -> deploy sidecar concurrency patch to edge pool (1h)
- oliver -> create subnet + NAT gw plan & IaC diff (4h)
- aisha -> enable S3 endpoint evaluation & cost estimate (today)
- matt -> add dashboard panels for NAT port utilization per NAT GW and per-subnet (2h)
- infra-bot -> keep monitoring and post when NATPortUtilization > 80% for any nat
sam: Rolling patch out to 25% canaries now, will monitor errors/port metrics.
aisha: Thanks — if canaries look good we'll ramp. Also let's throttle retries in the model loader to exponential backoff to avoid retry storms.
matt: FYI: if we need an emergency quick fix, we can spin up a NAT instance (EC2 with iptables SNAT) with multiple secondary IPs to increase port space temporarily, but that's more ops work.
oliver: Documenting the runbook steps in #runbooks/egress-nat for future incidents.
infra-bot: Post-incident checklist created and attached to INC-2026-1782.
aisha: Closing loop — so immediate: patch sidecar (sam), monitor NAT metrics (matt/infra-bot), prep NAT split (oliver). We'll reconvene in 90m or sooner if errors persist.
